topic: Ulm field RCT (arXiv, 28 Jul 2026): AI made fact-finding 29% faster but less correct, while summaries and idea drafts got faster and better
title: AI is fastest where you should trust it least

source.title: Faster, Higher, Stronger? The Impact of GenAI on Knowledge Work Productivity – Evidence from the Field
source.publisher: Bottesch et al., University of Ulm and KIT, arXiv:2607.25922

body:
About 25% of AI-assisted answers got a number wrong or made one up. The right figure was in the company's own files.

That is from a field experiment published on 28 July 2026. 128 staff at a large industrial firm did three real tasks, with or without an AI tool built on their own documents.

Most of us treat AI as the fast way to look things up. This study found that is where it slipped.

Finding facts: 29% faster with AI, and less correct.
Summing up a text: 52% faster, and better on 4 of 6 quality scores.
Drafting ideas: 39% faster, and better, but no more original.

The researchers think people trusted the tool and skipped the check. The speed hid the drop in quality.

What it does not mean: AI is bad at research. The tool was GPT-4o mini, tested in early 2025, at one company.

Today, when AI hands you a number, open the file it came from before you forward it.

Source: Bottesch et al., arXiv, 28 Jul 2026 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25922
action: when AI hands you a number, open the file it came from before you forward it
second_comment: One detail from the method that stuck with me: the AI tool was reading the same company files the right answers were in. So the wrong numbers were not a gap in the data. They were a gap in checking. Summaries and drafts are raw material you shape. A fact is something you pass on.

pages.headline: AI made them faster at finding facts, and less right
pages.deck: 128 staff at one industrial firm did three real tasks with and without AI. One result should change how you check its work.

pages.label: AI-assisted answers that misreported or made up a number
pages.body: The right figures were in the company files the AI tool was reading from. The wrong ones were handed in anyway.

pages.headline: Finding facts: faster, but less correct
pages.body: With AI, the fact-finding task took 29% less time. Scores for getting the facts right fell, both for numbers and for written details.

pages.headline: Summaries: faster and better
pages.body: Cutting a product text to four sentences or fewer took 52% less time with AI. Expert judges scored it clearly better on 4 of 6 quality measures.

pages.headline: Ideas: faster and clearer, not more original
pages.body: Drafting ideas took 39% less time. The ideas were more complete and better argued. Judges found no clear gain in how new they were.

pages.headline: Where the speed hid the problem
pages.left: The AI output is raw material. You still shape it, and quality went up.
pages.right: The AI output is the answer. The researchers think people took it as given, and accuracy fell.

pages.quote: Organizations implementing GenAI may hence face the risk of faster completion masking reductions in output quality.
pages.body: What it does not mean: AI is bad at research. The tool was GPT-4o mini, tested in early 2025, at one company.

pages.label: Do this today
pages.headline: Trace one number back to its file
pages.body: When AI hands you a figure, open the document it came from and find it yourself before you forward it. Drafts need a read. Facts need a check.

pages.headline: One idea, decoded, every week
pages.body: Plain English, a named source, and one thing to do with it.
